summary.en: A Punjab woman linked to a Pakistan-based handler carried out a railway-track blast in Rajasthan, killing two people and prompting the arrest of two suspects with alleged Pakistani handler ties. In Afghanistan, an unexploded ordnance blast in Ghazni killed one child and injured another, while fruit exports to Iran face delays of up to a month and Iran and Afghanistan have agreed to expand border crossings. India opened the Wagah crossing for Pakistani Sikh pilgrims, and a tanker was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz off Oman. The conflict recorded 1,794 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: En kvinne fra Punjab, knyttet til en handler i Pakistan, utførte en sprengning på jernbanespor i Rajasthan, der to personer ble drept, og to mistenkte med påståtte bånd til en pakistansk handler ble arrestert. I Afghanistan drepte en udetonert eksplosiv i Ghazni ett barn og såret et annet, mens frukt­eksporten til Iran får forsinkelser på opptil en måned, og Iran og Afghanistan har blitt enige om å utvide grenseovergangene. India åpnet Wagah-grensen for pakistanske sikh-pilgrimer, og en tank ble angrepet i Hormuzstredet utenfor Oman. Konflikten registrerte 1 794 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
background.extract: Since 2004, an insurgency has been fought in the Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by Islamist militant groups such as the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Jundallah, Lashkar-e-Islam (LeI), the Tehreek-e-Nafaz-e-Shariat-e-Mohammadi (TNSM), Al-Qaeda, and their Central Asian allies such as the Islamic State – Khorasan Province (ISKP), Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, East Turkistan Movement, Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, Ittihad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, and elements of organised crime. Before being transformed into an insurgency in 2017, the conflict was a war.
